notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the six change requirements (anchors, target dates, cells) and on all six dispositions (kept). disagreement: December boundary stay: A selects the active non-warranty contracts ending in December 2026 or 2027 (6 rows), B every contract ending in those Decembers that is not an active warranty (7 rows, adding the draft subscription 25); kept B's because it is the tighter boundary of the same selector. disagreement: adjacent-month boundary stay: A two requirements (November, January) whose cells hold OR-lists of LIKE predicates, B one requirement over all four months with cells {contract_type, status}; kept two requirements over the same nine rows, each selecting by an end_date GLOB, because a list of predicates means every predicate holds. The seed holds exactly six active warranty contracts ending in December 2026 or 2027 (100, 115; 60, 117, 33, 56), the six the originals name, so the originals cover the whole set. 'Approximately sixty days (2 calendar month)' is read as calendar-month arithmetic with end-of-month clamping, which every original target date uses; the only row where the two readings differ is 115 (28 Feb 2027 against 1 Mar 2027). Two original check names call December 2027 contracts 'December 2026'; the queries are right. No warranty contract with a non-active status ends in those Decembers and no active warranty ends in December of another year. Server-kept sys_updated_on is not a cell. revised: the three stays no longer repeat their selector's end_date GLOB in cells; the selector already fixes that column, so their cells are empty and their counts are unchanged.
